program_name: Master's Degree Programme in International Relations
campus: Rome, Luiss Guido Carli [uncertain - programme page only carries a generic university-wide sentence about facilities 'across Rome and Milan', not a programme-specific campus/building statement]

admission_type.eligible_applicants: Citizens of an EU or Schengen country, holding or about to hold a bachelor's degree by 18 November 2027
admission_type.test_or_certification: Luiss Test (written admission test); English B2 level assessed during the admission test
admission_type.number_of_choices_allowed: Up to two master's degree courses within the same subject area (Law/Political Science, which includes International Relations)

admission_type.eligible_applicants: Citizens of an EU (or Schengen) country who have completed or are about to complete a three-year degree programme qualifying for master's enrolment
admission_type.test_or_certification: GMAT with a minimum score of 515 (out of 805) OR GRE with a minimum score of 154 (out of 170) in both the Verbal and Quantitative sections

academic_requirements.prior_qualification: Bachelor's degree, obtained or to be obtained by the stated degree-completion deadline (18 November 2027 for the 2027/2028 EU/Schengen Luiss Test route)
academic_requirements.minimum_curricular_requirements: Direct/automatic eligibility for graduates of Italian degree classes L-36 (or 15, previous system) Political Science and International Relations; L-37 (or 35) Social Sciences for Cooperation, Development and Peace; L-16 (or 19) Public Administration; L-20 (or 14) Communication Sciences. Applicants from other degree classes may still apply if they have at least 48 university credits (earned or to be earned) across at least two of the following subject areas: Economics (SECS-P/01-06), Statistics (SECS-S/01-06), Law (IUS/01-14 and IUS/11-B), Linguistics, Political Science, Sociology, History and Politics.
academic_requirements.country_specific_rules: [uncertain] - not found on the pages retrieved for this programme; Luiss references country-specific evaluation only in the context of foreign qualification recognition (Declaration of Value / CIMEA), not a published country-by-country grade table for this course
academic_requirements.document_recognition: For applicants with a foreign qualification, Luiss requires either a Declaration of Value issued by the competent Italian consular representatives, or a CIMEA Certificate of Comparability or Verification; for holders of qualifications from Lisbon Convention signatory countries, the Diploma Supplement is accepted instead.

language_requirements.accepted_certificates: [uncertain] - Luiss confirms only that English is assessed at B2 level during the admission test; a dedicated list of accepted external certificates (IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge) with minimum scores specifically for the International Relations master's Luiss Test/GMAT-GRE routes could not be located with a direct quote in this pass (English-certificate score tables found via search belong to other Luiss schools - Business School and School of Government - which run separate admission processes, not the graduate-school International Relations programme)
language_requirements.exemptions: [uncertain] - not confirmed for this specific programme; not found on the retrieved pages

required_documents: Valid identity document (ID card or passport) showing citizenship - required at admission-test signup and again in PDF format at enrolment
Certificate of enrolment or degree certificate (transcript of records) showing exams taken, credits (CFU), field of study (SSD) and degree class - required for enrolment

Passport-sized front-facing photo (JPEG) - required at enrolment

Declaration of Value or CIMEA Certificate of Comparability/Verification (or Diploma Supplement for Lisbon Convention countries) - required for holders of foreign qualifications

source_quotes.quote: The degree class is LM-52
The annual single tuition fee for enrolment in the Master's Degree Programme in International Relations is € 15,000.00, divided into 3 instalments, plus the regional student welfare tax.
With many facilities across in Rome and Milan, Luiss stands out for its unique architectural spaces and large green study areas.
After a first semester of core courses, the program is divided into three majors: Diplomacy, Security, and Euro-Mediterranean Studies.
The Master's Degree Programme in International Relations is a two-year programme (120 ECTS). The first semester provides a solid theoretical and practical foundation common to all students.
You can take the Luiss Test if you are a citizen of an EU or Schengen country, with a bachelor's degree, either already obtained or to be obtained by 18 November 2027.
Candidates may specify up to two master's degree courses within the same subject area (Economics or Law/Political Science).
The participation fee is 150 euros.

Luiss offers the option to take the Admission Test in either Italian or English. Those choosing Italian will only be able to apply for courses taught in Italian, while English test-takers may apply for courses in both Italian and English.
Applications: December 2026 to 8 April 2027; Test Administration: 19-22 April 2027; Registration: By 22 June 2027; Bachelor's Degree Completion: By 18 November 2027
GMAT with a minimum score of 515 (out of 805), or GRE with a minimum score of 154 (out of 170) in the Verbal and Quantitative sections.
You can apply for only one of the available Master's degree courses. Your course choice is binding for admission, ranking, and subsequent enrolment.
From December 2026 to 31 March 2027 ... By 18 May 2027
at least 48 credits total university credits (earned or to be earned) in at least two of the following subject areas
At least a B2 level of English, which will be assessed during the admission test.
Admission procedures for Master's degree courses for non-EU/non-Schengen students for the 2027/2028 academic year are coming soon.
The admission notices, detailing all requirements, participation procedures, and the full calendar, will be available from November 2026.
The direct admission procedures with certifications for the 2026/2027 academic year are now closed.
A Declaration of Value issued by the consular representatives, or a CIMEA Certificate of Comparability or Verification. For Lisbon Convention signatories, the Diploma Supplement is accepted instead.
attach a copy of your valid ID (identity card or passport) in PDF format ... attach a copy of your health insurance card in PDF format (only for students residing in Italy)
upload your degree certificate or, alternatively, a duly signed self-certification.
First installment payment: June 15, 2026 (€5,000) ... Total annual fee: €15,000 (three installments)
The admission procedures for Master's degree courses for the 2027/2028 academic year are coming soon.
